Searched subject and both fixtures for FindingV1, FindingPayload, findingId, severity, ruleId, and a frameSchemas Finding payloadType. Zero hits in all cases. attacksRun.attack: NT-1 invents a Finding payload schema instead of an out-of-vocabulary frameType
attacksRun.detail: NT-1 is exactly the four delivery.v2 frameEnvelope required fields: protocolMajor, frameType, sequence, payload, with no optional fields (envelope declares optional []). protocolMajor 1 matches 'uint64; exactly 1'; sequence 0 matches 'starts at 0'. frameType Finding is absent from the 9-member closedWorkerToHostFrames, which I compared member-for-member against live delivery.v2 and found identical in content and order. The class is therefore carried by the frameType alone. Note the design is load-bearing: since payload is in the envelope's required list, omitting it would make the frame rejectable for a missing required field and would mask the property under test. The empty map keeps the out-of-vocabulary frameType the sole defect.

attacksRun.attack: NT-2 coverageCommitment omits the opensip.ts-provider.stage-coverage.v1 NUL domain separator
attacksRun.detail: Recomputed independently with a purpose-written RFC 8949 canonical encoder (definite length, major-type-0 unsigned integers, 0xf6 null, map keys sorted bytewise on the ENCODED key). SHA-256(UTF8('opensip.ts-provider.stage-coverage.v1') || 0x00 || cbor(entries)) = c1e7070edeafd1966749094fdda12d2bd0dd3f495c9674615e2efaf4eefe6d8c, an exact match to the fixture. I then computed the two failure variants to prove the separator was genuinely applied rather than coincidentally matched: bare entries with no domain yields 68e09421..., and domain-without-NUL yields 02a75770.... Both differ from the fixture value. The domain string matches delivery.v2 wireSchema.commitments.domains.stageCoverage verbatim and the construction matches commitments.domainRule verbatim.

attacksRun.attack: NT-2 is a coverage-domain mutation / takes over G23 NT-5
attacksRun.detail: The decisive test is the baseline, not the payload bytes. G21 NT-2's hostRequestedCoverageBaseline is one types/checked key at coverageState complete with deficiency null, identical to the payload entry, so there is no unknown-to-covered conversion. hostRequestedDomain carries exactly one key and entries carries exactly one matching entry, so there is no narrowing and no widening. Live product law v3 defines NT-5 as 'a Coverage payload that narrows, widens, or converts unknown to covered'; none of the three applies. Live g23-fixture-corpus.v3 NT-5 unknown-to-covered, by contrast, sets baseline unknown/provider-unavailable against a complete payload, which is the conversion this fixture deliberately does not perform. I confirmed by diff that G21 NT-2 differs from the g23.v3 NT-5 payload by exactly one added line, the findings member; sharing base bytes while testing an orthogonal invariant is not a takeover. Live provider-only-nt-gate-join.v6 records NT-1 and NT-2 with existingGate DR-G21 and NT-3 and NT-5 with existingGate 'none', so no G23-owned class is annexed.

attacksRun.attack: NT-2 does not actually exercise the unknown-field property (commitment silently absorbs the extra member)
attacksRun.detail: Constructed adversarially rather than accepted. Recomputing the commitment over the whole CoverageV1 map instead of entries yields cc9341a6..., which differs from the fixture value. This proves the extra findings member lies outside the commitment, so the host cannot detect the mutation through commitment arithmetic and rejection must come from closed-schema enforcement. That is precisely the NT-2 property. Live delivery.v2 CoverageV1 declares closed true with required exactly [analysisOrdinal, stageId, entries, coverageCommitment] and optional [], so findings is an unknown field on a closed payload. The subject's claim that the commitment is 'over entries only' and that the extra member is not included is measured true.

attacksRun.attack: Fixture bytes do not conform to the closed types they claim to transcribe
attacksRun.detail: Checked field-for-field against live delivery.v2. CoverageV1: all four required present, analysisOrdinal 0 matches 'uint64 exactly 0', stageId s-types matches the vector stageId. CoverageResultV1: all five required present (stageId, entryOrdinal, coverageState, key, deficiency); coverageState complete with deficiency null satisfies 'null exactly when coverageState=complete'. CoverageKeyV1: all eight required present and every value matches the live intra-universe-success-domain vector key byte-for-byte. hostRequestedDomain.subjectScope matches coverageDomain.vectorConstants.subjectScope exactly, and domainCommitment 9e1101a1... matches the live vector. Apart from the single deliberate extra member, the payload is a conforming instance.

decision.scopeOfAccept: Accepts g21-fixture-corpus.v1 as a CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED leftover-design fixture-authoring artifact under D-056 Decision 5, binding nothing. This is not a SATISFIED-GRADE cycle. The accept covers that the two authored fixtures conform to the already-closed delivery.v2 types they claim to transcribe, that the corpus's custody and negative claims are measured true, and that leftover-design of OBL-G21-FX-AUTHORING remains open. It does not qualify DR-G21, does not execute anything, does not satisfy DR-114 or DR-133, and does not authorize a recording.
decision.rationale: Seventeen attacks were run and all seventeen were refuted against live bytes. The freeze conditions hold exactly: subject 861bb4e7... at mode 0444 unmoved, both fixtures unmoved at 0444, HEAD 7e2284d0... matching the prompt and the subject's own head field. All 17 recordedInputs digests recompute with zero mismatches, and the subject satisfies its own remeasurementClause. The two substantive technical claims were verified by independent construction rather than inspection: I recomputed the NT-2 coverage commitment with a purpose-written RFC 8949 canonical encoder and obtained the fixture value exactly, and I computed the no-domain and no-NUL variants to prove the domain separator was genuinely applied rather than coincidentally matched. I also computed the commitment over the whole map to prove the extra findings member lies outside it, which is what makes NT-2 a real closed-schema unknown-field test rather than a disguised commitment-mismatch test. The sharpest available attack, that NT-2 annexes G23 NT-5, fails on the baseline: G21 NT-2 sets its coverage baseline equal to its payload, so no unknown-to-covered conversion occurs and cardinality is unchanged, which is orthogonal to all three NT-5 mutations in live product law v3, and live nt-gate-join v6 assigns NT-1/NT-2 to DR-G21 while leaving NT-3/NT-5 at existingGate none. Both fixtures conform field-for-field to the live closed CoverageV1, CoverageResultV1, CoverageKeyV1 and frameEnvelope definitions, and NT-1's empty payload is the correct minimal choice given payload sits in the envelope's required list. The corpus is scrupulous about what it does not do: leftoverDesignClosedIfAcceptedAndRecorded is empty, OBL-G21-FX-AUTHORING survives in five places, NT-6 is left unauthored even though D-145 routes it to DR-G21, and the candidate-buffer and subsequent-session evidence reserved by occupancy v4 EV-3 is left to execution. Four observations are recorded, the strongest being that 'unchanged from the closed complete types vector' describes a value the author computed rather than one delivery.v2 contains; none rises to SHOULD-FIX because the material claim each touches is measured true and reproducible from the subject's own stated recipe. Zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX survive verification.
